proposals.observation: Three CI workflows failed in the last 24 hours: Daily Blog Post (08:09), Funnel-Hack Digest (11:35), and Weekly Queue Topup (19:05). The content queue shows only 1 post queued against 47 published, meaning the pipeline is nearly empty. If Daily Blog Post continues failing, Joel's SEO publishing cadence stops entirely. The workflow failures are the single highest-leverage thing to triage today because every other system (email automation, quiz traffic) depends on fresh content arriving at the top of the funnel.
proposals.proposal: Joel needs to open each failed workflow run log in GitHub Actions and identify the root failure. The most likely cause, given all three failed on the same day with the queue almost depleted, is that the queue-topup job failed first (19:05 is a re-run timestamp, not necessarily the order of dependency), leaving the blog-post job with nothing to draft and the digest job with nothing to compile. Fix the Weekly Queue Topup workflow first, confirm it can write new entries to the queue file, then re-run Daily Blog Post manually. This is one triage session, not a code rewrite. The file path below is the topup workflow because that is the probable root cause, but Joel should not edit the workflow YAML itself (it is a blocked path) — instead he should inspect the run log and fix any upstream data source or API credential it depends on.
proposals.new_text:

proposals.impact: convert intro-load sessions into quiz starts
proposals.observation: The quiz shows 2 sessions in the last 48 hours, 0 starts, and 0 completions. Both sessions stalled at intro_load. That means visitors landed on the quiz page, the intro screen rendered, and every single one left before pressing any start button. This is a pure copy or friction problem on the intro screen, not a quiz logic problem.
proposals.proposal: Rewrite the quiz intro call-to-action so it tells the visitor exactly what happens when they press start, in concrete terms drawn from Joel's real client archetypes. Right now the intro almost certainly uses a generic promise. Replace it with something specific enough that a Money Avoidance person recognises themselves before they click. The intro is the quiz's only conversion moment and it is currently converting at 0%.

proposals.impact: lift 37.5% open rate toward Money Vigilance benchmark
proposals.observation: The Money Worship automation has a 37.5% open rate across 16 sends, against Money Vigilance at 66.67% (12 sends) and Money Avoidance at 52.63% (19 sends). Money Worship is the weakest sequence by a significant margin. Given that open rate is almost entirely determined by subject line (and preview text), the fastest fix is a subject line rewrite on the first email in the Money Worship sequence. No structural change to the automation, no re-segmentation — one subject line edit.
proposals.proposal: Replace the subject line on email 1 of the Money Worship sequence. The current line is likely aspirational or achievement-framed, which matches the Money Worship pattern on the surface but probably reads as congratulatory rather than creating the quiet tension that makes someone open. Money Worship subscribers believe their net worth and their self-worth are connected. The subject line should hold that specific tension, not celebrate it.
proposals.current_text: Subject: Your money results: Money Worship
proposals.new_text: Subject: When earning more doesn't feel like enough
